questions.question: A patient experiencing an asthma attack finds it much harder to move air into and out of their lungs. Which of the following physical changes in the respiratory system directly explains this sudden difficulty?
options: The alveoli fuse together, reducing the total surface area for gas exchange.
The bronchial tubes become constricted and narrower, increasing resistance to airflow.
The diaphragm muscle becomes temporarily paralyzed, preventing chest expansion.
The trachea completely collapses due to a lack of cartilage support.

questions.question: Why is a spacer device often recommended to be used alongside a metered-dose inhaler for delivering asthma medication?
options: It chemically alters the medication to make it more potent before it reaches the lungs.
It slows down the aerosol spray, helping more of the active medication reach the bronchial tubes instead of hitting the back of the throat.
It increases the volume of gas in the lungs, forcing the narrow airways to physically expand.
It filters out harmful air pollution and pathogens while the medicine is being inhaled.

questions.question: Consider four children with different profiles. Which child has the highest combination of recognized risk factors for developing asthma?
options: Child A: Born at a high birth weight, lives in a rural area with low pollution, and has no family history of allergies.
Child B: Born at a normal birth weight, lives in a city, and plays sports daily.
Child C: Born at a low birth weight, has a parent with asthma, and is regularly exposed to second-hand cigarette smoke.
Child D: Born at a normal birth weight, has a food allergy, and lives in a smoke-free home in the countryside.

questions.question: Malaria is caused by a protozoan parasite and is transmitted between humans by mosquitoes. Influenza is caused by a virus and spread through airborne droplets. Why are both classified as infectious diseases?
options: Because they both damage the lungs and circulatory system of the host.
Because they both can be transmitted from one host organism to another, either directly or via a vector.
Because they are both caused by non-living environmental toxins that enter the body.
Because they can both be treated and cured using the exact same type of antibiotic medication.

questions.question: A doctor treats two patients: one has tuberculosis (caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis) and the other has chickenpox (caused by the Varicella-zoster virus). What do the causative agents of these two diseases have in common?
options: They are both cellular organisms that can replicate independently outside of a host.
They are both pathogens that invade host organisms and disrupt normal body functions.
They are both susceptible to standard antibacterial drugs like penicillin.
They are both non-living genetic particles wrapped in a protein coat.

questions.question: A person diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes (a non-infectious autoimmune condition) lives with their family. Why is there no risk of the family members catching diabetes from close contact with this person?
options: The family members must have already developed immunity to the diabetes pathogen.
Diabetes is caused by a virus that can only be transmitted through blood transfusions, not casual contact.
Non-infectious diseases do not involve a transmissible pathogen that can replicate and pass between hosts.
The medication used to treat diabetes completely sterilizes any pathogens before they can spread.

questions.question: Two individuals have the same genetic background. Individual X eats a diet high in saturated fats and sugar and has a sedentary desk job. Individual Y eats a balanced diet and jogs three times a week. How do their lifestyles affect their long-term health risks?
options: Individual X has a higher risk of developing infectious cardiovascular diseases than Individual Y.
Individual X's sedentary lifestyle and unbalanced diet increase their risk of developing non-infectious conditions like Type 2 diabetes.
Individual Y's high activity level completely eliminates any genetic risk of disease.
Individual Y is more susceptible to viral infections because of the physiological stress of exercise.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes how substance use (such as smoking or heavy alcohol consumption) contributes to the development of lifestyle diseases?
options: It introduces beneficial pathogens that strengthen the immune system against chronic conditions.
It causes immediate, temporary physiological changes that leave no long-term chemical footprints in tissues.
It introduces harmful chemicals that can cause cumulative damage to organs and alter metabolic processes over time.
It guarantees that a person will develop a chronic disease within a predictable five-year window.

questions.question: A public health campaign aims to reduce the incidence of coronary heart disease and liver disease in a population. Which combination of lifestyle recommendations would be most effective?
options: Increasing the consumption of processed foods while reducing daily physical activity to rest the heart.
Avoiding tobacco smoke, limiting or avoiding alcohol intake, and maintaining a balanced diet with regular physical activity.
Replacing all water intake with caffeinated energy drinks and focusing solely on anaerobic weight training.
Relying entirely on daily vitamin supplements while continuing to smoke and drink heavily.

questions.question: Why are substances like caffeine in coffee, nicotine in tobacco, and alcohol in beer classified as recreational drugs?
options: They are consumed primarily for non-medical, personal pleasure or social reasons and affect the way the body or mind works.
They are only capable of producing positive health outcomes without any risk of side effects or addiction.
They are synthesized in laboratories specifically to treat infectious bacterial diseases.
They do not alter brain chemistry or affect a person's central nervous system.

questions.question: How do the primary effects of stimulants and depressants on the central nervous system compare?
options: Stimulants and depressants both speed up the transmission of electrical impulses, but stimulants target the muscles while depressants target the brain.
Stimulants increase neurotransmitter activity to speed up body systems, whereas depressants reduce neurotransmitter activity to slow down body systems.
Stimulants slow down heart rate to increase mental focus, while depressants speed up digestion to promote relaxation.
Stimulants physically block nerve pathways, while depressants create new synaptic connections between neurons.

questions.question: In a reaction-time test, a volunteer who has consumed a depressant substance takes significantly longer to press a button when a red light flashes. What is the cellular explanation for this observation?
options: The nerve impulses travel faster along the sensory neurons but are blocked at the muscles.
The depressant slows down the transmission of signals across synapses in the brain and spinal cord.
The depressant causes the light receptors in the eyes to stop functioning temporarily.
The skeletal muscles of the finger have been temporarily depleted of glucose.

questions.question: A person who has consumed excessive amounts of alcohol over many years is diagnosed with cirrhosis of the liver and cognitive decline. Why are these specific organs severely affected?
options: The liver is responsible for breaking down toxic alcohol, leading to long-term tissue scarring, while the brain's delicate neural pathways are damaged by chronic exposure to this depressant.
The liver and brain are the only organs in the body that contain receptors for alcohol molecules.
Alcohol physically blocks the blood vessels leading directly to the brain and liver, causing oxygen deprivation.
The liver converts alcohol into a nutrient that over-nourishes brain cells, causing them to grow out of control.

questions.question: A driver drinks a strong cup of black coffee containing caffeine before a long night drive. How does this stimulant chemically benefit the driver's immediate performance?
options: It dilates the pupils to allow infrared light in, improving night vision.
It increases alertness and shortens reaction times, allowing the driver to process hazards and brake more quickly.
It acts as a pain reliever, preventing muscle fatigue in the legs and hands.
It slows down heart rate, helping the driver stay calm and meditative during traffic.

questions.question: Cocaine and ecstasy are classified as illegal stimulants. What is a key physiological risk associated with these substances due to their stimulant properties?
options: They can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure and slow the heart rate to a stop.
They can cause severe over-stimulation of the cardiovascular system, leading to abnormally high heart rates and blood pressure.
They put the user into a deep, unresponsive sleep by suppressing the respiratory center in the brain.
They destroy the body's ability to produce adrenaline, leaving the user permanently fatigued.

questions.question: Why do many people find it extremely difficult to stop smoking tobacco, even when they are fully aware of the severe damage it causes to their lungs?
options: Tobacco smoke contains physical fibers that bind tightly to the alveoli, creating a physical dependency.
Nicotine in the tobacco leaves triggers chemical changes in the brain's reward system, making it highly addictive.
The tar in cigarettes acts as a sedative that relaxes the chest muscles, making breathing without it feel painful.
Carbon monoxide in the smoke is required by the red blood cells to transport oxygen efficiently.

questions.question: How does long-term exposure to tobacco smoke contribute to the development of both respiratory diseases (like COPD) and circulatory diseases (like heart disease)?
options: Tobacco smoke contains pathogens that infect both the alveoli and the heart valves directly.
Toxic chemicals in smoke damage the airways and alveoli, while also damaging blood vessels and increasing plaque build-up in arteries.
Carbon monoxide in smoke converts oxygen into carbon dioxide before it can reach the body's vital organs.
Smoking causes the lungs to expand so much that they physically compress and damage the surrounding heart tissue.

questions.question: Why is inhaling the fumes of substances like glue or spray paint (solvent abuse) considered highly dangerous, even from the very first use?
options: Solvents contain heavy bacterial loads that cause immediate, severe lung infections.
The inhaled chemicals can cause sudden heart failure, suffocation, or permanent brain damage due to their toxic effects on the body.
Solvents are highly acidic and immediately dissolve the cartilage of the trachea upon contact.
They cause the body to rapidly lose water, leading to fatal dehydration within minutes.

questions.question: Many people switch from smoking traditional cigarettes to vaping, believing it to be entirely harmless. What is a key health concern that remains when a person vapes?
options: Vaping still delivers nicotine, which is highly addictive and has negative cardiovascular and neurological effects on the body.
E-cigarettes contain the exact same concentration of tar and carbon monoxide as burning tobacco leaves.
Vaping completely destroys the user's immune system within a few days of use.
The water vapor from e-cigarettes causes the alveoli to fill up with liquid, simulating drowning.

questions.question: In the mid-20th century, smoking was often marketed as healthy, but today it is strictly regulated due to its known health risks. How does this shift reflect the nature of scientific inquiry?
options: Scientific facts are completely random and change based on which political party is in power.
As new, rigorous evidence from long-term health studies emerged, scientists updated their understanding of smoking's harmful effects.
The chemical composition of tobacco plants naturally mutated over time to become toxic to humans.
Early scientists were not allowed to perform experiments, so they had to guess the health effects of smoking.

questions.question: During an asthma attack, a patient struggles to breathe. What physical change is occurring within their respiratory system to cause this immediate difficulty?
options: The diaphragm muscle becomes paralyzed and cannot contract to pull air in.
The bronchial tubes narrow due to muscle contraction and inflammation.
The alveoli lose their elasticity and permanently collapse, reducing the surface area.
The trachea becomes completely blocked by hard calcified deposits.

questions.question: Four children are being monitored by a pediatrician. Based on known risk factors, which child has the highest risk of developing asthma?
options: Child A: Born at a normal weight, lives in a rural area with low pollution, has no family history of asthma.
Child C: Born at a normal weight, has a balanced diet, exercises daily, but has a cousin with asthma.
Child B: Born with low birth weight, lives in a highly polluted city, and has a mother who smoked during pregnancy.
Child D: Born with high birth weight, lives in an area with clean air, but has a mild allergy to strawberries.

questions.question: A doctor is treating two patients. Patient X has tuberculosis (caused by a bacterium) and Patient Y has cardiovascular disease (linked to diet and inactivity). How do the causes of these diseases compare?
options: Patient X's disease is caused by a cellular pathogen, whereas Patient Y's disease is non-infectious and arises from physiological changes due to lifestyle.
Both are caused by living cellular pathogens that reproduce inside the host's body.
Patient X's disease is caused by an environmental toxin, while Patient Y's disease is caused by a non-living virus.
Both diseases are infectious because they can be passed from person to person through close physical contact.

questions.question: A student with asthma accidentally shares a water bottle with a classmate. The classmate is worried they might 'catch' asthma. Why is this fear scientifically unfounded?
options: Asthma is only transmissible between close biological relatives through direct contact.
Asthma is caused by a virus that can only be transmitted through the air, not through shared liquids.
Sharing water bottles only transmits bacterial diseases, and asthma is caused by a fungal infection.
Asthma is a non-infectious disease, meaning it is not caused by transmissible pathogens and cannot be passed from person to person.

questions.question: How does the lifestyle choice of long-term cigarette smoking simultaneously increase the risk of diseases in both the gas exchange system and the circulatory system?
options: It damages the alveoli in the gas exchange system and causes narrowing and hardening of arteries in the circulatory system.
It increases the volume of the lungs while decreasing the heart rate to dangerously low levels.
It introduces infectious pathogens that destroy lung tissue and directly block the valves of the heart.
It liquefies the pleural membranes and decreases the production of red blood cells.

questions.question: An individual consistently consumes a diet high in saturated fats and sugar while maintaining a highly sedentary desk job. What is the physiological consequence of this lifestyle on their risk of disease?
options: The body overproduces white blood cells to combat the excess nutrients, leading to infectious immune responses.
The lungs must work twice as hard to expel unused nutrients, causing chronic swelling of the trachea.
The lack of physical exertion and excess energy intake can lead to fat deposition in blood vessels, increasing the risk of cardiovascular disease.
The digestive system stops absorbing minerals, resulting in immediate infectious bacterial growth in the blood.

questions.question: A patient with a family history of heart disease wants to take proactive steps to minimize their risk of developing this lifestyle-related condition. Which set of daily habits would be most effective?
options: Replacing all solid foods with fruit juices, avoiding exercise to prevent heart strain, and drinking moderate spirits.
Engaging in regular aerobic exercise, eating a balanced diet low in saturated fats, and avoiding smoking and alcohol.
Eating a high-calorie diet to boost metabolism, sleeping 12 hours a day, and taking preventative antibiotics.
Smoking low-tar cigarettes instead of regular ones and relying solely on vitamin supplements without changing physical activity levels.

questions.question: A scientist is studying two unnamed recreational drugs. Drug A increases heart rate and makes the user feel hyper-alert. Drug B slows down the transmission of nerve impulses, leading to delayed reactions. How should these drugs be classified?
options: Both Drug A and Drug B are stimulants because they are used recreationally.
Drug A is a depressant; Drug B is a stimulant.
Drug A is an infectious agent; Drug B is a chemical analgesic.
Drug A is a stimulant; Drug B is a depressant.

questions.question: Why is it extremely dangerous to operate heavy machinery or drive a vehicle after consuming a depressant drug?
options: Depressants cause the muscles to contract uncontrollably, leading to sudden involuntary movements.
Depressants drastically accelerate thought processes, causing the brain to overlook physical obstacles.
Depressants slow down the nervous system, significantly increasing the time it takes to perceive a hazard and apply the brakes.
Depressants impair peripheral vision by temporarily paralyzing the optic nerve.

questions.question: Alcohol is a widely available, legal recreational drug. However, what are the well-documented physiological risks associated with long-term, excessive consumption of alcohol?
options: Permanent structural damage to the brain and severe scarring of the liver tissue.
Accelerated nerve regeneration in the spinal cord and improved memory retention.
Increased efficiency of the gas exchange system and strengthening of the bronchial walls.
Sudden conversion of liver cells into muscle tissue, leading to abdominal rigidity.

questions.question: How do stimulant drugs temporarily alter a person's cognitive and physical performance?
options: They decrease the speed of electrical impulses along motor neurones to prevent muscle fatigue.
They slow down the heart rate, allowing the brain to rest and think more deeply.
They increase alertness and can lead to quicker thinking and faster physical reaction times.
They block all sensory inputs, allowing the person to focus purely on memory retrieval.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the dual impact of chronic substance abuse on an individual's overall health?
options: It damages physical organs but has absolutely no effect on brain chemistry or mental well-being.
It causes severe physical damage to organs such as the liver or lungs, and can also lead to mental health issues like anxiety, depression, or addiction.
It improves physical endurance while causing temporary, minor mental confusion that resolves instantly.
It causes mental health issues only if the drug is illegal; legal substances have no physical or mental health risks.

questions.question: Many people who smoke tobacco express a strong desire to quit but find it incredibly difficult to do so. What chemical explanation accounts for this difficulty?
options: Tobacco leaves contain nicotine, a highly addictive chemical that alters brain chemistry and creates a strong dependency.
Carbon monoxide in tobacco smoke binds irreversibly to muscle cells, causing physical cravings.
Tar coats the taste buds, making food taste unpleasant unless nicotine is present in the bloodstream.
The smoke contains specialized bacteria that colonize the brain and demand more tobacco.

questions.question: A heavy smoker is diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and is warned by their doctor about their elevated risk of heart disease. Why are both of these conditions linked to smoking?
options: The smoke blocks the digestive tract, preventing nutrients from reaching the heart and lungs.
Smoking introduces pathogens that infect the heart valves while inflating the lung volume.
Inhaling tobacco smoke damages the delicate structures of the gas exchange system and also negatively affects the cardiovascular system.
Tobacco smoke contains high levels of carbon dioxide which permanently replaces all oxygen in the blood.

questions.question: A teenager is found inhaling fumes from a container of industrial glue in an attempt to experience altered perception and intoxication. What is this hazardous practice called?
options: Stimulant therapy
Herbal inhalation
Solvent abuse
Therapeutic vaporization

questions.question: Why is solvent abuse considered an extremely high-risk behavior, even if tried only once?
options: It causes an instant, irreversible bacterial infection in the digestive tract that resists all antibiotics.
It permanently stops the body's ability to absorb water, leading to rapid dehydration within hours.
It causes the lungs to expand to twice their normal size, making breathing impossible.
It can cause immediate fatal heart failure (sudden sniffing death) or lead to permanent, long-term damage to the brain and kidneys.

questions.question: During inhalation, how do the muscles of the respiratory system cooperate to bring air into the lungs?
options: The diaphragm relaxes and moves upwards while the rib cage moves downwards, increasing air pressure in the lungs.
The diaphragm contracts and flattens while the intercostal muscles move the rib cage up and out, increasing lung volume and lowering pressure.
The lungs actively contract like muscles to squeeze air in from the windpipe.
The abdominal muscles push upwards on the heart, forcing the lungs to expand sideways.

questions.question: How are healthy human lungs structurally adapted to maximize the efficiency of gas exchange?
options: They have millions of tiny alveoli providing a massive surface area, extremely thin walls for short diffusion paths, and a rich capillary blood supply.
They contain a single, large, thick-walled air sac that keeps gases compressed under high pressure.
They are lined with thick muscular tissue to actively pump oxygen directly into the main arteries.
They have a dry, impermeable surface that prevents water vapor from slowing down the movement of gases.

questions.question: Many people switch from smoking traditional cigarettes to using e-cigarettes (vaping) believing it is entirely harmless. What shared chemical risk exists in both vaping and smoking?
options: Both deliver tar, which instantly blocks the main bronchi.
Both produce high levels of carbon monoxide that turn the lungs black.
Both rely on burning tobacco leaves to release active chemicals.
Both involve the consumption of nicotine, an addictive and health-detrimental substance.

questions.question: Initially, some early reports suggested vaping might carry no long-term health risks. Over time, as more clinical trials and patient data are collected, medical guidelines are being revised. What fundamental scientific principle does this demonstrate?
options: Once a scientific theory is published, it can never be questioned or changed.
Scientific ideas are constantly updated, refined, or changed as new, reliable evidence emerges.
Older scientific studies are always completely false and should be ignored.
Scientific consensus is decided by public votes rather than empirical evidence.

questions.question: During an asthma attack, what physical change happens to the breathing (bronchial) tubes that makes breathing difficult?
options: They dilate and become filled with excess oxygen.
They narrow, restricting the passage of air.
They lengthen and lose their connection to the alveoli.
They permanently dissolve due to severe inflammation.

questions.question: Which of the following combinations represents only risk factors that can increase the likelihood of developing asthma?
options: High birth weight, a high-fiber diet, and regular cardiovascular exercise.
Air pollution, family history of asthma, and having an allergy.
Bacterial infections, a high-sugar diet, and a lack of physical activity.
Excess consumption of caffeine, solvent abuse, and low dietary iron.

questions.question: Why can flu (influenza) be passed from person to person, whereas a condition like coronary heart disease cannot?
options: Flu is caused by pathogens like viruses, while coronary heart disease is non-infectious.
Flu is caused by a lack of exercise, while heart disease is caused by airborne bacteria.
Flu only affects the digestive system, whereas heart disease affects the respiratory system.
Flu is a lifestyle disease, whereas heart disease is an inherited genetic mutation.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes infectious diseases from non-infectious diseases?
options: Infectious diseases can be passed from one organism to another, while non-infectious diseases cannot.
Infectious diseases are only caused by lifestyle factors, while non-infectious diseases are caused by pathogens.
Non-infectious diseases can spread through coughing, while infectious diseases are purely genetic.
Non-infectious diseases always develop instantly, while infectious diseases always take years to show symptoms.

questions.question: How do an unbalanced diet and a lack of physical exercise affect a person's health over time?
options: They decrease the body's susceptibility to infectious pathogens like viruses.
They can increase the risk of developing non-infectious lifestyle diseases.
They directly cause immediate narrowing of the bronchial tubes.
They guarantee that a person will develop infectious diseases of the lungs.

questions.question: Which set of actions is most effective for preventing the development of lifestyle diseases?
options: Regular exercise, a balanced diet, avoiding smoking, and avoiding alcohol.
Taking daily prescription medicines, avoiding caffeine, and reducing sleep.
Using inhalers, increasing calorie intake, and reducing physical activity.
Replacing smoking with solvent inhalation and eating high-fat meals.

questions.question: How are recreational drugs primarily classified based on their general physiological effects on the central nervous system?
options: Legal drugs and illegal drugs.
Depressants and stimulants.
Natural substances and synthetic chemicals.
Solid substances and gaseous inhalants.

questions.question: A person takes a recreational drug and experiences slowed thinking and delayed reaction times. What class of drug did they most likely consume?
options: A stimulant.
A depressant.
An antibiotic.
A vaccine.

questions.question: Which of the following is a legal depressant that, when used heavily over a long period, can cause severe damage to both the brain and the liver?
options: Caffeine
Nicotine
Alcohol
Cocaine

questions.question: How do stimulants affect the body's functioning?
options: They slow down thinking and significantly increase reaction times.
They make you feel more alert and can give you quicker thinking and reaction times.
They lower your heart rate and cause immediate muscle relaxation.
They prevent the absorption of oxygen in the alveoli.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs contains only illegal stimulants used as recreational drugs?
options: Cocaine and ecstasy
Caffeine and nicotine
Alcohol and glue
Nitrous oxide and aspirin

questions.question: What is the main reason why smoking tobacco is highly addictive and has powerful physical effects on the body?
options: It contains high amounts of carbon dioxide.
Tobacco leaves naturally contain nicotine, a very addictive substance.
The smoke contains paint thinner and solvents.
It contains caffeine, which stimulates the heart.

questions.question: Regular smoking of tobacco leaves is a major risk factor for which group of diseases?
options: Asthma, COPD, lung cancer, and heart disease
Type 1 diabetes, food allergies, and influenza
Brain damage, liver cirrhosis, and measles
Common cold, malaria, and food poisoning

questions.question: What is 'solvent abuse'?
options: Drinking excessive amounts of liquid stimulants like coffee and energy drinks.
Misusing liquid prescription medicines to cure infectious bacterial diseases.
Inhaling vaporized chemical substances to become intoxicated.
Consuming contaminated water containing pathogens.

questions.question: Which of the following groups contains only common household or industrial substances that are misused in solvent abuse?
options: Paint thinner, glue, and nitrous oxide
Nicotine, caffeine, and alcohol
Cocaine, ecstasy, and tobacco
Aspirin, inhaler medicine, and water

questions.question: Why is it vital for survival that oxygen is continuously absorbed into the human body and carbon dioxide is removed?
options: Oxygen is needed for respiration to release energy, while carbon dioxide is a toxic waste product that must be cleared.
Oxygen cools down the brain, while carbon dioxide is used to build muscle tissue.
Oxygen is converted directly into blood cells, while carbon dioxide prevents blood from clotting.
Oxygen is needed to digest food, while carbon dioxide is required to inflate the lungs.

questions.question: Which of the following is an adaptation of healthy lungs that increases the rate and amount of gas exchange?
options: A small surface area combined with thick, dry cell walls in the bronchi.
A very large surface area and thin, moist walls in the alveoli.
Narrowing of the bronchial tubes to build up air pressure.
A rigid muscular structure that prevents blood flow around the air sacs.

questions.question: A student claims that 'vaping is completely safe because it does not involve burning tobacco leaves.' Why is this claim incorrect?
options: Vaping still involves consuming nicotine, which is detrimental to health.
Vaping contains high levels of caffeine, which slows down the heart.
Vaping introduces pathogens like bacteria directly into the liver.
Vaping has been proven to cause identical liver damage to long-term alcohol use.

questions.question: What is the current scientific consensus regarding the long-term health effects of vaping?
options: The long-term health effects are completely known and proven to be harmless.
The health effects of vaping are not yet fully known.
Scientists have proven vaping has absolutely no effect on the heart or lungs.
Vaping is known to cure existing lung conditions like asthma and COPD.

questions.question: In science, why might advice about the safety of products like e-cigarettes (vaping) change over several decades?
options: Because scientific ideas are updated as new evidence emerges.
Because manufacturers are allowed to rewrite scientific laws.
Because the human gas exchange system evolves completely every few years.
Because old scientific studies are automatically deleted after ten years.
